00Doctoral Research · Interview

Emergent Narrative
Through Unreliable Information

Trust, social propagation, and consequence permanence in autonomous agent systems. A study of how agents that lie, misremember, and pursue private agendas produce behaviour a human observer reads as a story.

Ritwik SharmaMA Game Design, UAL23 June 2026
01The problem

Two ways to make narrative.
Both fail in opposite directions.

Scripted

Branches authored in advance. Meaningful, but brittle and finite. The player eventually sees the edges of the authored space, and the cost grows exponentially with freedom.

Procedural

Events generated stochastically. Endlessly varied, but semantically thin. Things happen; they do not mean. Emergent history, not emergent story.

The space between them is underexplored. My research proposes a third model: autonomous agents with private motivations, partial information, and social relationships, where the driver under investigation is information reliability itself. The central question:

How do agents with private motivations, unreliable information, and social relationships produce narrative behaviour that human observers recognise as coherent and meaningful?

02The gap in the literature

Not a degree of difference.
A category difference.

The closest neighbour is Ryan et al.'s Talk of the Town (2016), which models gossip, memory fallibility, and lying in a social network. The distinction is structural, and it is the whole basis of this research:

Existing work

Deception is probabilistic and affinity-driven. A character transmits false information based on how much they like their interlocutor; the misinformation is drawn at random. The lie is incidental.

This research

Deception is agenda-driven and temporally deferred. An agent plants a lie on Day 1 and queues a consequence for Day 3. You are caught not because the tip was wrong, but because a trap was built around your belief. The lie is strategic; the consequence is irreversible.

No existing framework treats strategic information distortion as the primary driver of emergent narrative. That is the gap, and it is one of category, not degree.

03Research questions

Four questions, one instrument.

RQ1How does information reliability variance affect the structural properties of emergent social networks?
RQ2What trust-modelling mechanisms are necessary and sufficient to produce behaviour observers perceive as socially coherent?
RQ3How does consequence permanence, the irreversibility of actions, interact with reliability to shape the felt quality of narrative?
RQ4Can a parameterised framework characterise the relationship between architecture configurations and narrative-coherence outcomes, yielding design principles?
04The research instrument

Measuring the gap between
belief and ground truth.

Every agent holds an epistemic state: what it believes happened, filtered through trust, personality, and instinct. The Watcher sits above the simulation holding perfect ground truth, with no trust, no agenda, no ability to act. It measures how far each agent's belief has drifted from reality.

distortion=(hops × 0.20) + ((1 − confidence) × 0.50)

Mapped as a network over time, it is a structural coherence metric assessable without full human evaluation. Deterministic underneath, so the same configuration reproduces the same run.

belief drifts from truth as it travels
An epistemic gap, made measurable: the distance between what is true and what a system believes is true.
05Live · reproducible

The instrument, running.

A seeded, reproducible simulation: seven agents form their own account of an event while the Watcher records the truth. Same seed, same run, every time. This is the working core the PhD formalises into a rigorous instrument.

06Evidence at scale

The hard parts are
already built.

I am not starting from zero. A production system, Zombita, has implemented the core research concepts at scale, with real people, for years, before the research question was formally articulated. It is the evidence that the architecture is buildable and that the social layer holds up outside a lab.

  • RQ1UUID-based agent identity, persistent choice tracking, social-graph structure.
  • RQ2A nightly reputation pipeline reading seven days of behaviour into trust archetypes.
  • RQ3Consequence permanence: irreversible economic burn, permanent debt, data that never deletes.

Phase 1 is formalisation of working code, not greenfield construction.

production · the nightly reputation pipeline, live
06bEvidence · operations

Not a character. An administrator.

The clearest sign the system is real, not roleplay: it does genuine operational work. It reads its own server logs, recognises a security-exploit pattern, advises on configuration, and diagnoses resource problems in plain language, all from live state.

This is the deployed proof that the agent operates on real, current information about a running system, which is the same capability the research formalises: an agent reasoning from an imperfect, live picture of its world.

live · recognising a security-exploit pattern from the logs
live · diagnosing server resource usage
07Architecture

A deterministic engine,
with a language surface.

A deliberate methodological choice: the epistemic engine is rule-based and deterministic. Identical configurations produce identical narrative logs, which is what makes the human-evaluation phase valid.

The core concepts were developed 2018–2022, before LLMs were a default tool. The architecture was built from first principles, not in response to what LLMs can do. So generative models are treated honestly: not a foundation, but one component to evaluate empirically, gated on playability and real-time performance. Swap the model for a classical NLP layer and the system still runs. What changes is fluency, not function.

07bEvidence · the memory engine

It doesn't just remember.
It forms a view.

Every night, unprompted, the system folds the day's activity into a permanent summary and consolidates it into a living document of what it believes to be true. That is memory: the four-layer architecture from the proposal, running in production.

daily log→summary→consolidate→living document

But it goes one step past memory. From that belief-state it forms its own reading of what is happening, and why, and offers a judgement. That step, from a model of the world to a view on it, is the core of RQ2: interpretation under partial information, which is exactly what the research measures.

Humans then rate the take (good call / off). The loop closes.

web · her nightly read, and her opinion on it
web · the living document she maintains, versioned
database · the belief-state, written by sonnet, unedited
terminal · the consolidation running, live

09The role of play

Reading the room
is the research.

The research is practice-based: the player is placed inside the unreliable-information problem and survives by interpreting the social environment. Who is honest, who is an informant, what a rumour will cost three days from now. Interpretation under risk is the instrument.

In the deployed system this is already live: a physical NPC with rule-based perception, named shopkeepers wired to a closed-loop economy, and a give-flow routed through the same identity and authorize gate as everything else.

10Planned research environments

What's next, stated as next.

To keep the line clean: the engine, the simulation, and the deployment are running today. The two purpose-built research environments are fully designed as game-design documents, but not yet built:

  • PSPrison Sandbox (Unity), a closed social system. NPCs carry undisclosed truth rates; you infer reliability through interaction, not UI.
  • USUntamed Shadows (Unreal), open territory, faction-driven information agendas. Tests whether the framework generalises across a structurally different social system.

Each is scoped as a targeted research prototype, not a commercial game. The simulation you saw is their logic, already proven.

Prison Sandbox · concept, not yet built
11Method & ethics

Mixed methods.
Honest about what's measured.

Method

Phase 1: formalise the rule-based architecture. Phase 2: parameter sweeps with the Watcher, varying reliability, trust decay, and consequence permanence. Phase 3: a within-subjects human study rating narrative logs for coherence, meaning, and believability. Determinism makes the sweeps reproducible.

Ethics

Human-evaluation protocols go to institutional ethics review before recruitment. Participants assess fictional simulation logs, not real social scenarios; no deception of participants is involved. Members of the deployed community consent at entry to a researched, agent-run environment.

rule-based corereproducible · seededLLM = surface, evaluated empiricallyethics review before recruitment
12Contribution

The contribution,
and one honest question.

A formal agent architecture for reliability-stratified information behaviour; an engine-agnostic simulation framework made publicly available; a reproducible measurement instrument, the Watcher and distortion score; and empirical data on how information reliability shapes perceived narrative coherence.

The question did not come from a literature review. It came from building the same idea, in production, for years, and only lately finding the formal frame for it.
